name: glow-bright
concept: A soft glow pulses while the element also brightens slightly, combining light and luminance. Use it for an active or lit-up state that needs a touch more punch than a plain glow.

name: glow-luminous
concept: The element brightens and casts a wider soft light at the same time, for a gentle luminous idle state. Use it when an element should feel lit from within, not just outlined.

name: glow-radiant-wide
concept: A dim brightness rise pairs with a wide, diffuse halo that spreads well past the element edges. Use it for a prominent idle highlight that should read as radiant, not sharp.

name: glow-brighten-quick
concept: The element brightens sharply along with a tight glow, on a short cycle. Use it for a small element that needs a crisp, noticeable idle pulse of light.

name: glow-luster
concept: A moderate glow and brightness rise combine for a lustrous, polished idle shine. Use it for elements that should feel premium or softly lit, like a badge or icon.

name: glow-shine-soft
concept: A faint brightness lift joins a narrow glow for a very soft, barely-there shine. Use it where a hint of life is wanted without drawing much attention.

name: glow-bloom-fade
concept: The glow blooms quickly then fades slowly back to rest, an asymmetric rhythm unlike a smooth sine pulse. Use it when the light should feel like it switches on fast and lingers.

name: glow-fade-bloom
concept: The glow builds slowly then fades quickly, the reverse asymmetric rhythm of a fast bloom. Use it for a light that feels like it gathers gradually then snaps off.

name: glow-fast-bloom
concept: The glow blooms almost instantly to a wide halo then fades slowly over most of the cycle. Use it for a state that should flash into light and dissolve gently.

name: glow-ember
concept: Brightness and glow build slowly like a warming ember, then fade quickly, on a longer cycle. Use it for a warm, smoldering idle light rather than a crisp pulse.

name: glow-swell
concept: The glow swells up early in the cycle and eases back down, an uneven rhythm rather than a symmetric pulse. Use it for a light that feels like it swells and recedes.

name: glow-simmer
concept: Two small glow bumps occur per cycle, like a simmering light rather than one smooth pulse. Use it for a quietly active state that flickers with light twice per beat.

name: shimmer-sheen
concept: A quick, subtle brightness rise pairs with a slight opacity dip, like a sheen passing over the surface. Use it for a light shimmer distinct from a moving highlight sweep.

name: shimmer-glint
concept: A brief, sharp brightness spike suggests a glint of light catching the surface. Use it for a small, fast shimmer that reads as a quick catch of light.

name: shimmer-veil
concept: A faint brightness rise combines with a whisper of blur, like a veil of light passing over. Use it for a soft, hazy shimmer rather than a crisp one.

name: shimmer-quick
concept: Brightness rises and falls fast and barely, a minimal shimmer for constant background motion. Use it where the shimmer must stay in the background, almost unnoticed.

name: shimmer-flutter
concept: Brightness flutters up and down twice in quick succession, like light catching an uneven surface. Use it for a shimmer with an irregular, fluttering rhythm.

name: shimmer-glaze
concept: Brightness and saturation both lift slightly together, giving a glazed, glossy shimmer. Use it for a surface that should look faintly glazed or polished as it idles.

name: shimmer-subtle
concept: A tiny brightness change, barely perceptible, keeps an element quietly alive. Use it for the most understated shimmer available, for calm interfaces.

name: shimmer-drift
concept: Brightness and a faint hue shift drift slowly together, like light slowly drifting across a surface. Use it for a slower, dreamier shimmer with a hint of color movement.

name: focus-breathe
concept: A tiny blur breathes in and out, like the element softly loses and regains focus. Use it for a dreamy, ambient idle state on a calm interface.

name: soft-focus-drift
concept: A faint blur and a slight brightness dip drift together, like attention softly drifting out of focus. Use it for a slow, contemplative ambient loop.

name: dreamy-blur-pulse
concept: A small blur rises with a light opacity dip, for a dreamy, hazy pulse of soft focus. Use it where an element should feel gently unreal or floating in a dream.

name: hazy-breathe
concept: A gentle blur breathes between a light haze and a deeper one, never fully sharp. Use it for a constantly soft, hazy idle presence.

name: blur-dream
concept: A soft blur grows alongside a barely-there scale increase, for a slow dreamlike swell. Use it for an element that should feel like it gently drifts closer and softer.

name: blur-soft-focus
concept: A very slight blur comes and goes on a short cycle, the lightest soft-focus breathing available. Use it for a quick, quiet hint of ambient motion.

name: blur-veil-breathe
concept: A soft blur breathes together with a faint glow, like a veil of light and haze. Use it for an ambient state that combines softness with a gentle inner light.

name: glow-breathe
concept: The element grows very slightly while a soft glow rises and falls, like breathing light. Use it for an idle state that should feel calmly alive.

name: glow-pulse-soft
concept: A faint scale increase joins a small brightness rise for a soft, gentle pulsing glow. Use it for a subtle idle pulse that barely moves.

name: glow-scale-breathe
concept: A slow, gentle scale grow accompanies a soft glow, on a longer breathing cycle. Use it for a calmer, slower breathing-and-glowing idle state.

name: glow-gentle-swell
concept: The element swells early in the cycle with a rising glow, then eases back slowly. Use it for a soft surge of light and size rather than a steady pulse.

name: glow-drift-scale
concept: A slow scale grow and a gentle brightness rise drift together over a long cycle. Use it for a very calm, slow ambient presence with a hint of size change.

name: two-stage-glow
concept: The glow brightens, holds briefly at its peak, then fades, instead of a smooth sine pulse. Use it when the light should feel deliberate, with a clear pause at full glow.

name: glow-flash-hold
concept: The element flashes brightly and glows, holds that peak briefly, then fades slowly away. Use it for a stronger two-stage glow that reads as a deliberate flash.

name: glow-step-pulse
concept: The glow rises in two steps to a wider peak, holds, then fades, rather than one smooth curve. Use it for a layered, stepped light build.

name: glow-brighten-hold
concept: Brightness rises, holds briefly at its peak, then eases back down, a two-stage brightness pulse. Use it for a state that should feel like it pauses at full brightness.

name: glow-two-beat
concept: Two short glow beats fire close together, then the element rests for the remainder of the cycle. Use it for a light that pulses twice like a heartbeat, then pauses.

name: aura-slow
concept: A soft glow rises and falls over many seconds, an unhurried aura rather than a quick pulse. Use it for a calm, meditative idle presence.

name: aura-deep
concept: A wide glow and a gentle brightness rise build deeply over a long cycle, like a deep aura of light. Use it for a strong but very slow ambient presence.

name: aura-meditative
concept: A soft blur and a wide glow rise together over a very long cycle, almost meditative in pace. Use it for the calmest, slowest ambient state in the set.

name: aura-drift
concept: A slow scale grow and a wide glow drift together over several seconds. Use it for an aura that feels like it slowly expands and recedes.

name: aura-long
concept: Brightness alone rises and falls over a long cycle, a pure light aura with no shadow spread. Use it where only a slow glow of brightness is wanted, without a halo.

name: aura-calm
concept: A very faint glow barely rises over a long, calm cycle, the quietest aura available. Use it for the most understated ambient presence, almost imperceptible.

name: glow-wide
concept: A wide, diffuse halo spreads well beyond the element on each pulse, more spread out than a tight glow. Use it for an element that should cast a broader soft light.

name: glow-diffuse
concept: A large, soft-edged halo diffuses outward on each pulse, softer and wider than a standard glow. Use it for a gentle, cloud-like spread of light.

name: glow-halo-wide
concept: A broad box-shadow halo pulses around the element's full outline, wider and more even than a drop-shadow glow. Use it for a boxed or pill element that needs a rounded halo.

name: glow-spread
concept: The glow spreads out to a very large, soft radius before fading, wider than most glows in the set. Use it for a dramatic but still gentle ambient spread.

name: glow-halo-soft
concept: A gentle brightness rise joins a wide, soft halo for an even, diffuse lit look. Use it for an element that should feel softly and broadly lit at once.

name: shimmer-flicker
concept: Brightness flickers rapidly and irregularly at low amplitude, faster and fainter than a normal shimmer cycle. Use it for a faint, nervous flicker of light rather than a smooth pulse.

name: glow-slow-radiance
concept: A very large, soft halo builds over a long, unhurried cycle, the widest and slowest glow in the set. Use it for a rare, dramatic ambient radiance that takes its time.
